summary.text: COBSWAIT is a small batch utility that pauses a job step. It ACCEPTs an 8-character value from SYSIN, moves it to the binary field MVSWAIT-TIME and CALLs the external routine MVSWAIT with it, then ends with STOP RUN. The header comment states the value is a wait time in centiseconds. It has no files, no conditions and no business logic; it is executed by job step WAIT in app/jcl/WAITSTEP.jcl.

paragraphs.name: (PROCEDURE DIVISION entry)
paragraphs.logic: ACCEPTs PARM-VALUE (PIC X(8)) from SYSIN, moves it to MVSWAIT-TIME (PIC 9(8) COMP), CALLs 'MVSWAIT' USING MVSWAIT-TIME and issues STOP RUN.

no_business_rules_reason: COBSWAIT is a technical batch utility: it reads a wait duration from SYSIN and calls the external routine MVSWAIT to suspend the step. It contains no decisions, validations, calculations or data processing with business meaning.

observations.text: The SYSIN value is moved from alphanumeric PIC X(8) to numeric PIC 9(8) COMP without a NUMERIC check; a non-numeric or short (space-padded) value gives an unpredictable wait time.
The header says 'PARM IN CENTISECONDS' but the value is read from SYSIN, not from the EXEC PARM; the unit (centiseconds) is stated only in the comment and depends on MVSWAIT.
MVSWAIT is an external called routine with no source in the repository (external-or-missing).

sme_questions.question: Where does MVSWAIT come from (site or vendor load library) and what unit does it expect for MVSWAIT-TIME?
